record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the computational power of the advice class CL/poly, and is there a natural syntactic characterization of it?

evidence.quote: Problem 18. What is the power of CL/poly, and does it have a natural syntactic characterization?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A catalytic Turing machine is a deterministic Turing machine equipped with three tapes: a read-only input tape, a read/write work tape, and a read/write auxiliary "catalytic" tape. The catalytic tape is initialized with an arbitrary string τ (the catalyst); the machine may freely read and overwrite the catalytic tape during its computation, but at the end of every computation, on every input and for every initial catalyst τ, the catalytic tape must be restored to exactly its initial content τ. The machine's output on input x must be the same for every initial catalyst τ.

Define catalytic logspace CL as the class of languages decidable by a catalytic Turing machine that uses O(log n) cells on the work tape and at most n^c cells on the catalytic tape, for some constant c, on inputs of length n, in time polynomial in n.

For a complexity class C, the advice class C/poly is the class of languages L such that there exists a sequence of advice strings {α_n}_{n≥0} with |α_n| ≤ p(n) for some polynomial p, and a language L' ∈ C, with x ∈ L if and only if ⟨x, α_{|x|}⟩ ∈ L'.

Problem:
(a) Determine the computational power of CL/poly, i.e., characterize which languages lie in CL/poly, and locate this class relative to standard complexity classes (such as L/poly, NL/poly, P/poly, ZPP, etc.).
(b) Give a natural syntactic characterization of CL/poly (for example, in terms of a uniform machine model, circuit family, or algebraic computation model) that does not refer explicitly to non-uniform advice strings.
artifact.status_search_result: Catalytic logspace remains an active area of investigation. Recent works (2024–2025) establish unconditional collapses such as CL = CNL = CPrL and characterize lossy catalytic computation, and explicitly note that techniques extend to catalytic classes with advice, but no source provides a complete characterization of the power of CL/poly nor a natural syntactic (advice-free) description of it. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
status_evidence.snippet: CL = CNL = CPrL... collapses unconditional for polynomial-size catalyst and logarithmic free space.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on the structure of CL, but does not characterize CL/poly.

status_evidence.title: Fully Characterizing Lossy Catalytic Computation (ECCC TR24-138)
status_evidence.snippet: Results on lossy catalytic computation likely extend to CSPACE with advice.
status_evidence.claim: Catalytic classes with advice are noted as a direction but no characterization of CL/poly is given.

status_evidence.title: The Structure of Catalytic Space: Capturing Randomness
status_evidence.snippet: Studies catalytic logspace and its relationships with randomized and nondeterministic variants.
status_evidence.claim: No syntactic characterization of CL/poly is established.
